title: UNIT 4: TRIGONOMETRIC FUNCTIONS
notes: ✓ Trigonometry → the study of relationships between angles and sides of triangles.

title: 4.1 ANGLES & STANDARD POSITION
notes:
✓ Angle → a measure of rotation of a ray about its vertex.

◆ Initial side → the original position of the ray.

◆ Terminal side → the final position after rotation.

◆ Vertex → the point about which the ray rotates.

✓ Positive angle → anticlockwise rotation.

✓ Negative angle → clockwise rotation.

✓ Angle in standard position → vertex at the origin and initial side on the positive x-axis.

Example: 1125° = 3(360°) + 45°, so its terminal side is coterminal with 45°.

title: DEGREE & RADIAN MEASURE
notes:
✓ Degree → 1/360 of one complete revolution.

✓ Radian → the angle subtended at the center of a circle by an arc whose length equals the radius.

Fundamental relation:
✓ π rad = 180°
✓ 2π rad = 360°

Degrees → radians:
✓ θ(rad) = θ° × π/180°

Radians → degrees:
✓ θ° = θ(rad) × 180°/π

Example: 120° = 120 × π/180 = 2π/3 rad.

Example: 4π/3 rad = 4π/3 × 180°/π = 240°.

title: ARC LENGTH & RADIAN FORMULA
notes:
For a circle of radius r, if an angle θ is measured in radians:

✓ Arc length:
l = rθ

✓ Therefore:
θ = l/r

◆ r → radius
◆ l → arc length
◆ θ → central angle in radians.

Example: If r = 5 cm and θ = 2 rad, then l = rθ = 5(2) = 10 cm.

title: COTERMINAL ANGLES
notes:
✓ Coterminal angles → angles having the same initial side and the same terminal side.

In degrees:
✓ θc = θ ± 360°n

In radians:
✓ θc = θ ± 2πn

where n is an integer.

Example:
30° + 360° = 390°
30° − 360° = −330°
Therefore, 390° and −330° are coterminal with 30°.

✓ Coterminal angles have the same trigonometric values.

title: BASIC TRIGONOMETRIC FUNCTIONS
notes:
For an acute angle θ in a right triangle:

✓ sinθ = opposite/hypotenuse
✓ cosθ = adjacent/hypotenuse
✓ tanθ = opposite/adjacent

Reciprocal functions:
✓ cscθ = 1/sinθ = hypotenuse/opposite
✓ secθ = 1/cosθ = hypotenuse/adjacent
✓ cotθ = 1/tanθ = adjacent/opposite

Example: If opposite = 12, adjacent = 5 and hypotenuse = 13:
sinθ = 12/13
cosθ = 5/13
tanθ = 12/5.

title: SIGNS IN THE FOUR QUADRANTS
notes:
The signs of the main trigonometric functions are:

◆ Quadrant I → sin +, cos +, tan +
◆ Quadrant II → sin +, cos −, tan −
◆ Quadrant III → sin −, cos −, tan +
◆ Quadrant IV → sin −, cos +, tan −

Remember:
✓ Q I → all positive
✓ Q II → sine positive
✓ Q III → tangent positive
✓ Q IV → cosine positive.

Example: If sinθ > 0 and cosθ < 0, θ lies in Quadrant II.

title: REFERENCE ANGLE
notes:
✓ Reference angle θR → the positive acute angle between the terminal side of an angle and the x-axis.

For a coterminal angle between 0° and 360°:

◆ Q I: θR = θ
◆ Q II: θR = 180° − θ
◆ Q III: θR = θ − 180°
◆ Q IV: θR = 360° − θ

Example: θ = 245°
θR = 245° − 180° = 65°.

✓ The absolute values of trigonometric functions of an angle and its reference angle are equal; the sign is determined by the quadrant.

title: COMPLEMENTARY & SUPPLEMENTARY ANGLES
notes:
✓ Complementary angles → angles whose sum is 90°.

If α + β = 90°:
✓ sinα = cosβ
✓ cosα = sinβ
✓ tanα = cotβ

Example:
sin(90° − θ) = cosθ.

✓ Supplementary angles → angles whose sum is 180°.

✓ sin(180° − θ) = sinθ
✓ cos(180° − θ) = −cosθ
✓ tan(180° − θ) = −tanθ

Example:
sin150° = sin30° = 1/2.

title: TRIGONOMETRIC FUNCTIONS OF NEGATIVE ANGLES
notes:
For an angle θ in standard position:

✓ sin(−θ) = −sinθ
✓ cos(−θ) = cosθ
✓ tan(−θ) = −tanθ

✓ Sine and tangent are odd functions.
✓ Cosine is an even function.

Example:
sin(−30°) = −1/2
cos(−30°) = √3/2
tan(−45°) = −1.

title: PERIODICITY
notes:
✓ A periodic function repeats its values at regular intervals.

Sine:
✓ sin(θ + 2πn) = sinθ
✓ Period = 2π or 360°
✓ Domain = all real numbers
✓ Range = [−1, 1]

Cosine:
✓ cos(θ + 2πn) = cosθ
✓ Period = 2π or 360°
✓ Domain = all real numbers
✓ Range = [−1, 1]

Tangent:
✓ tan(θ + πn) = tanθ
✓ Period = π or 180°
✓ Domain excludes θ = (2n + 1)π/2
✓ Range = all real numbers.

Example:
sin780° = sin(720° + 60°) = sin60° = √3/2.

title: GRAPHS OF SIN, COS & TAN
notes:
y = sinθ → smooth wave between −1 and 1; period = 2π.
Key points over one period:
(0,0), (π/2,1), (π,0), (3π/2,−1), (2π,0).

 y = cosθ → smooth wave between −1 and 1; period = 2π.
Key points:
(0,1), (π/2,0), (π,−1), (3π/2,0), (2π,1).

 y = tanθ → repeating increasing curves; period = π.
Vertical asymptotes occur at:
θ = (2n + 1)π/2.

✓ For graphing, use θ in radians on the x-axis and the function value on the y-axis.

title: TRIGONOMETRIC IDENTITIES
notes:
Fundamental Pythagorean identities:

✓ sin²θ + cos²θ = 1
✓ 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ
✓ 1 + cot²θ = csc²θ

These identities come from the Pythagorean theorem and the reciprocal definitions.

Example:
If sinθ = −3/5 and θ is in Quadrant III:
cos²θ = 1 − sin²θ
= 1 − 9/25
= 16/25
Since cosine is negative in QIII:
cosθ = −4/5.

title: ADDITION & DOUBLE-ANGLE IDENTITIES
notes:
Addition identities:

✓ sin(A + B) = sinA cosB + cosA sinB
✓ sin(A − B) = sinA cosB − cosA sinB

✓ cos(A + B) = cosA cosB − sinA sinB
✓ cos(A − B) = cosA cosB + sinA sinB

Double-angle identities:

✓ sin2θ = 2sinθ cosθ

✓ cos2θ = cos²θ − sin²θ
✓ cos2θ = 1 − 2sin²θ
✓ cos2θ = 2cos²θ − 1

✓ tan2θ = 2tanθ/(1 − tan²θ)

Example:
sin75° = sin(45° + 30°)
= sin45°cos30° + cos45°sin30°
= (√2/2)(√3/2) + (√2/2)(1/2)
= (√6 + √2)/4.

title: HALF-ANGLE IDENTITIES
notes:
Half-angle identities:

✓ cos(θ/2) = ±√((1 + cosθ)/2)

✓ sin(θ/2) = ±√((1 − cosθ)/2)

✓ The sign depends on the quadrant of θ/2.

Example:
cos15° = cos(30°/2)
= √((1 + cos30°)/2)
= √((1 + √3/2)/2)
= √(2 + √3)/2.
